questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: Considering the reaction, which step in a radical chain generates the first radicals?

options.text: Homolytic cleavage of a weak bond by light or heat

options.misconception: that is not a radical step

questions.explanation: Initiation produces radicals by homolytic cleavage of a weak bond, such as a peroxide oxygen-oxygen bond, under light or heat; propagation then consumes and regenerates radicals and termination combines two radicals.
questions.hint: Light or heat splits a weak bond homolytically.

provenance.author: orgchem2-bank-author
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: Considering the reaction, why does HBr add anti-Markovnikov to an alkene in the presence of peroxides?

options.text: The peroxide changes the alkene geometry
The reaction proceeds through the more stable carbon radical
Bromine adds first as Br plus

questions.explanation: A bromine radical adds to the alkene so that the more stable carbon radical forms, and that radical then abstracts hydrogen from HBr; this radical chain gives anti-Markovnikov orientation unlike the ionic mechanism.

provenance.author: orgchem2-bank-author
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: Considering the reaction, which C-H bond is most reactive toward radical chlorination?

options.misconception: methyl is a type of primary
aryl C-H bonds are very strong

questions.explanation: Radical chlorination abstracts the hydrogen that leads to the most stable radical, so tertiary C-H bonds react faster than secondary, which react faster than primary, reflecting radical stability even though chlorine is not highly selective.

provenance.author: orgchem2-bank-author
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: Considering the reaction, which radical is most stabilized?

options.misconception: primary is less stable than benzylic

questions.explanation: A benzylic radical is strongly stabilized by resonance delocalization into the aromatic ring, making it more stable than simple alkyl radicals, while vinylic radicals are unusually hard to form.

provenance.author: orgchem2-bank-author
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: Considering the reaction, what role does tributyltin hydride play in radical reductions?

options.text: It initiates by forming oxygen radicals
It donates a hydrogen atom to a carbon radical
It acts as a radical inhibitor

questions.explanation: Tributyltin hydride transfers a hydrogen atom to a carbon radical in a propagation step, converting the radical into a reduced alkane while generating a tin radical that continues the chain.
questions.hint: Tin hydride is a hydrogen atom donor.

provenance.author: orgchem2-bank-author
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: Considering the reaction, what is the propagating species in free-radical polymerization of an alkene?

options.text: A carbocation at the chain end
A carbanion at the chain end
A carbon radical at the growing chain end

questions.explanation: In free-radical polymerization an initiator radical adds to a monomer to create a new carbon radical at the chain end, which adds successively to more monomer units in repeated propagation steps until termination occurs.
questions.hint: A chain-end carbon radical propagates growth.

provenance.author: orgchem2-bank-author
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: Considering the reaction, why does adding a radical inhibitor stop a chain reaction?

options.text: It converts active radicals into stable non-radical species

questions.explanation: A radical inhibitor reacts rapidly with chain-carrying radicals to give stable species or low-reactivity radicals, terminating propagation and preventing the chain from continuing even though monomers remain.

provenance.author: orgchem2-bank-author

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: Considering the reaction, which reagent selectively brominates the allylic position of an alkene?

options.misconception: that gives addition across the alkene
that adds HBr to the double bond

options.text: Bromine in carbon tetrachloride in the dark

questions.explanation: N-bromosuccinimide maintained at low concentration under radical initiation conditions abstracts an allylic hydrogen, and the resonance-stabilized allylic radical captures bromine to give allylic bromination without adding across the double bond.

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: Considering the reaction, what is the typical geometry at a simple alkyl radical center?

It donates a hydrogen atom to a carbon radical

questions.explanation: Tributyltin hydride transfers a hydrogen atom to a carbon radical in a propagation step, converting the radical into a reduced alkane while generating a tin radical that continues the chain.
questions.hint: Tin hydride is a hydrogen atom donor.

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: In the laboratory, what is the propagating species in free-radical polymerization of an alkene?

options.text: A carbon radical at the growing chain end
A carbocation at the chain end
A carbanion at the chain end

questions.explanation: In free-radical polymerization an initiator radical adds to a monomer to create a new carbon radical at the chain end, which adds successively to more monomer units in repeated propagation steps until termination occurs.
questions.hint: A chain-end carbon radical propagates growth.

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: In the laboratory, why does adding a radical inhibitor stop a chain reaction?

options.text: It converts active radicals into stable non-radical species

questions.explanation: A radical inhibitor reacts rapidly with chain-carrying radicals to give stable species or low-reactivity radicals, terminating propagation and preventing the chain from continuing even though monomers remain.

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: In the laboratory, which reagent selectively brominates the allylic position of an alkene?

options.misconception: that gives addition across the alkene
that adds HBr to the double bond

options.text: Bromine in carbon tetrachloride in the dark

questions.explanation: N-bromosuccinimide maintained at low concentration under radical initiation conditions abstracts an allylic hydrogen, and the resonance-stabilized allylic radical captures bromine to give allylic bromination without adding across the double bond.

questions.stem: In the laboratory, which ring size forms most readily in a radical cyclization?

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: In the laboratory, what is the typical geometry at a simple alkyl radical center?

options.misconception: that is typical of carbocations with sp hybridization

options.text: Square planar at the radical carbon

questions.explanation: A simple alkyl radical is approximately trigonal planar with the unpaired electron in a p orbital, so attack can occur from either face, which often erodes stereochemical information at that center.

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: For the structure shown, which step in a radical chain generates the first radicals?

options.text: Homolytic cleavage of a weak bond by light or heat

options.misconception: that is not a radical step

questions.explanation: Initiation produces radicals by homolytic cleavage of a weak bond, such as a peroxide oxygen-oxygen bond, under light or heat; propagation then consumes and regenerates radicals and termination combines two radicals.
questions.hint: Light or heat splits a weak bond homolytically.

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: For the structure shown, why does HBr add anti-Markovnikov to an alkene in the presence of peroxides?

options.text: The peroxide changes the alkene geometry

Bromine adds first as Br plus

questions.explanation: A bromine radical adds to the alkene so that the more stable carbon radical forms, and that radical then abstracts hydrogen from HBr; this radical chain gives anti-Markovnikov orientation unlike the ionic mechanism.
